copy.headline: ‘This will affect me greatly’: Transit users question rideshare cuts across Fort Worth
copy.caption: Trinity Metro’s board of directors approved cuts to the agency’s On-Demand program that eliminate some areas from service. Paul David Williams wonders how he will get home with his groceries.

story.summary: Trinity Metro’s board of directors approved cuts to the agency’s On-Demand program that eliminate some areas from service. Enjoy reading the news again. Join over 110,000 neighbors who count on our newsletters for stories happening in your backyard. Sign up for free . Paul David Williams wonders how he will get home with his groceries. The 70-year-old south Fort Worth resident, who lives on a fixed Social Security income, is upset that Trinity Metro transit agency approved changes Monday to the On-Demand microtransit service that will eliminate the closest grocery store to his home from the Southside zone. Williams said he will be forced to walk with his groceries two blocks from the Walmart Neighborhood Market at 717 W.
